Subject: Post-demo: Calcite evaluation plan & prompt collection

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: Validate model fit for Calcite's summarization + QA flows against your live docs and customer transcripts.
- Success metrics you mentioned: ROUGE-style overlap for summaries, targeted BLEU-like scores on structured QA, and a subjective quality bar for hallucination < 2% on sample set.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We send a short prompt/edge-case template (attached) that your team can populate with 30–50 representative prompts and 10–15 edge cases (PII, truncated inputs, long-context threads).
2) Once we receive the populated CSV, we'll run an initial benchmark on 2 model families and share a short report + example outputs.
3) If results look promising, we schedule a 1-hour evaluation review with your ML/ops team and discuss rollout options (hosted vs dedicated).

Model recommendations (initial): Llama-3-13B-q4f for latency-sensitive infra and Llama-3-70B-q4f for highest-quality outputs; we can also try Mistral-Instruct-7B as a cost-efficient baseline. We'll include quantized variants in the benchmark.

I've attached a prompt_samples_template.csv to make the intake easy and calcite_ma_plan.pdf with a suggested mutual action plan. Can you and Jose confirm who will own the prompt upload and whether any of the examples will contain customer PII? If yes, we'll provide redaction guidance.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

- The prompts will include real customer support transcripts; some contain email addresses and order IDs (PII). We cannot share raw PII.
- Timeline: we can populate the template by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-09) if that works.

Question on models: can you include a small-run of conversational-context tests (6–8k tokens) — we need to understand latency and cost impact on long-turn conversations. Also, do you have any pre-built redaction scripts or recommended redaction strategy?

Appreciate it — Alyssa

Perfect — thanks for confirming Jose as the owner. A few quick answers: 

- Redaction: we have a short redaction checklist and simple Python script snippets that strip email addresses, phone numbers, and order IDs and optionally replace named entities with tokens (e.g., <PERSON>, <ORDER_ID>). I'll paste minimal guidance below and Marissa will attach the redaction checklist and SOC2 summary.
- Long-context tests: yes — we'll include 6k and 8k token runs in the benchmark. For cost/latency tradeoffs we'll show per-token latency and per-request cost across the model variants.

Redaction guidance (brief): 
- If you cannot share raw PII, replace 1:1 with deterministic tokens (e.g., <EMAIL_1>, <ORDER_23>) so we preserve referential integrity across prompts.
- Remove or truncate any content that would identify the customer at an organization-level (company names that would deanonymize).
- For transcripts where redaction removes critical context, add an explicit note in the CSV comment column so we can flag these for manual review.

Marissa/Ben — can you attach the redaction checklist and SOC2 summary to this thread?

Best — Hannah
